title: Stellar activity demotes GJ 9404 b to a planetary candidate
summary: GJ 9404 is a nearby M dwarf ($d=23.8\,\text{pc}$), around which a $13.4586^{+0.0044}_{-0.0067}\,\text{d}$ planet has been claimed in a recent study using 54 publicly available HARPS-N radial velocities (RVs). We re-analyse the spectroscopy associated with this study, and carry out a joint modelling of: (i) stellar rotation in RV, FWHM, and Mount Wilson S-index through Gaussian processes; (ii) long-term trends in all physical quantities; (iii) planetary signals in RV. Current evidence supports the existence of planets in the period range $2-100\,\text{d}$ by at most $Δ\ln Z=-0.4$ for any considered stellar-activity model, which is insufficient for a widely accepted planet detection. Additional spectroscopy is necessary to accurately quantify the stellar activity of GJ 9404 and determine whether any RV signals warrant further attention.

title: Searching for substellar companion candidates with Gaia IV. New planetary-mass companions found in debris disks
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics - Number of pages: 21 - Number of figures: 11 (including multipanel figures)
summary:
When spatially resolved, debris disks often exhibit structures (gaps, rings, and spirals) that may indicate the presence of unseen planetary-mass companions. However, such planets have not been detected in most cases. Gaia opens a new mass-separation parameter space for detecting unseen planets. A tool named GaiaPMEX has been developed to detect and characterize companions to stars. It is based on two binarity indicators derived from DR3: the Gaia astrometric signature and, when the sources were also observed by Hipparcos, the Gaia-Hipparcos proper motion anomaly.
  We used GaiaPMEX on 94 stars hosting resolved debris disks to search for companions. When companions were identified, we combined GaiaPMEX results with high-contrast imaging and radial velocity data to further constrain their mass and orbital properties.
  We found stellar or substellar companions around five targets (HD 54341, HD 146897, HD 206893, HD 107146, and HD 106906) and indications (2 sigma) for companions around three additional targets (BD+45 598, TWA 7, and HD 120326). The companion to the 150 Myr star HD 107146, which harbors a ring-like dust disk, is found to be a 2-6 Jupiter-mass planet orbiting between 2-10 au. A massive 3-20 Jupiter-mass companion is found 3-10 au from the close binary HD 106906, which already hosts a remote planet orbiting at more than 700 au, and an edge-on disk. The tentative companions to TWA 7 and HD 120326 are planetary-mass companions at 1-3 au. Both stars host a multiple-ring system. We finally provide meaningful upper limits on the possible presence of companions in the range of 0-100 au around a few emblematic stars (49 Cet, AU Mic, beta Pic, and epsilon Eri) and stars hosting well-defined ring-like structures.

title: The Effect of Dust Grain Growth and Stellar Metallicity on Gas Giant Planet Formation by Disk Instability
comment: 24 pages, 1 table, 7 figures, in press, ApJ
summary: The formation of gas giant planets by the gas disk gravitational instability (GDGI) mechanism depends sensitively on the thermodynamics of the protoplanetary disk gas: disk gas must be able to cool on orbital timescales for dense clumps to become gravitationally unstable and contract to form protoplanets. Since disk cooling is regulated by the opacity of the dust grains embedded in the gas, the properties of these dust grains are critical for the GDGI mechanism. Grain growth to larger sizes than assumed in traditional opacity models for solar metallicity, as well as protostars with sub-solar metallicity, should have lower opacity disks that are more conducive to planet formation by GDGI. Here we use a three dimensional radiative hydrodynamics and gravitation code to compute the evolution of the GDGI in $0.091 M_\odot$ disks with varied initial minimum values (1.3 to 2.7) of the Toomre criterion orbiting solar-mass protostars. Three sets of eight models are computed: one with the standard opacity, and two more with the opacity reduced by arbitrary factors of 10 or 100. As expected, the reduced opacity models result in enhanced disk fragmentation by the GDGI and the production of more self-gravitating clumps than the standard opacity models. Nevertheless, all three opacities form similar self-gravitating clumps at this early phase of clump evolution, with masses of 0.2 to 0.7 $M_{Jup}$ and semimajor axes between 6 and 13 au. Significant dust grain growth should enhance the ability of the GDGI to form protoplanets around super-solar metallicity protostars.

title: IGRINS-2 Reveals an Oxygen-rich Dayside Atmosphere of WASP-12 b: Resolving the C/O Controversy
comment: 12 pages, 8 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: Recent studies have shown that measurements of hot-Jupiter atmospheric composition, including carbon-to-oxygen (C/O) and refractory-to-volatile (R/V) abundance ratios, provide powerful diagnostics of the chemistry and formation of gas giant planets. Important questions remain about the atmospheric composition of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-12 b: its dayside C/O ratio remains under debate, and its R/V ratio is not yet well constrained. We present high-resolution (R $\sim$ 45,000) near-infrared dayside emission spectroscopy of the ultra-hot Jupiter WASP-12 b with IGRINS-2 on Gemini North during post-eclipse phases. Cross-correlation analysis reveals volatile molecular signals of H$_2$O and CO together with tentative signals of OH and gas-phase refractories in the planetary atmosphere. The planetary signals appear in emission, indicating a thermal inversion in the dayside atmosphere. A chemically consistent Bayesian retrieval yields C/O $=0.72^{+0.08}_{-0.10}$, disfavoring carbon-rich dayside solutions with C/O $>1$ at greater than $5σ$. This independent, line-resolved measurement supports an oxygen-rich atmosphere, providing a new constraint on the long-standing C/O controversy surrounding WASP-12 b. Our retrieval also yields a host-star-normalized R/V ratio, $[\mathrm{R/V}]_{*}=0.17^{+0.22}_{-0.23}$, which is consistent with those of other ultra-hot Jupiters similarly characterized with IGRINS/IGRINS-2. Although the sample remains small, this consistency suggests a shared atmospheric chemistry among these planets, potentially reflecting similar proportions of accreted volatile and refractory material.

title: Obliquity of Mercury with a fluid core and a deformable mantle
summary:
In anticipation of BepiColombo's orbital insertion in 2026, this study revisits the rotation of Mercury, modelling it with a fluid core and a deformable mantle. For this well-established physical model, we provide an analytical solution based on a novel Lagrangian formalism. Our approach enables a comprehensive 3D solution for the mantle's orientation, including the phase in longitude at the perihelion. The model incorporates dissipative torques from core-mantle boundary friction and tidal deformations, conservative pressure torques, and the effect of the planet's apsidal precession.
  We validate the equilibrium positions obtained numerically in previous studies, but identify discrepancies in earlier analytical works. These inconsistencies overestimated the out-of-Cassini-plane offset induced by tidal deformation by a factor of 100. Additionally, we explore the parameter space to determine where the spin axis deviates most from the Cassini plane and identify a region exhibiting bifurcation in the spin axis equilibrium position. This region cannot be adequately analysed using a model linearised with respect to the obliquity angle.

title: The First Adolescent Super-Earth-Sized Multi-Planet System Around an M Dwarf: TOI-2079
comment: 22 pages, 15 figures, 2 tables, accepted for publication in ApJL
summary: We identify two planets in close-in orbits around the M-type star TOI-2079 as the first super-Earth-sized planets orbiting a multi-planet M dwarf with a well-determined age of $1$-$2$\,Gyr. The interior planet, TOI-2079 b, has an orbital period of $1.49232359^{+0.00000099}_{-0.00000086}$ d, and the outer planet, TOI-2079 c, has an orbital period of $9.3174523\pm0.0000098$ d. The host star characterization is based on spectroscopic observations, which classify it from an M1.5 to an M3.5 dwarf with an effective temperature of $3695\pm77$ K. Further analysis determined TOI-2079's rotation period to be $17.33^{+0.29}_{-0.28}$ d. Multiple ground-based follow-up observations, combined with a state-of-the-art validation procedure, allow us to rule out possible astrophysical false-positive scenarios and validate the planetary nature of both objects. We find that the inner planet has a radius of $1.320\pm0.050 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 867\pm27$ K, while the outer planet has $R_{\rm p} = 1.671\pm0.051 R_{\oplus}$ and $T_{\rm eq} = 473\pm15$ K.

title: The GAPS programme at TNG. LXXXIII. Orbital refinement and atmospheric investigation of TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b)
comment: Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)
summary: TOI-1518 b (BD+66 1610 b) is a highly irradiated ultra-hot Jupiter on a strongly misaligned orbit, a benchmark target for atmospheric and dynamical studies. We comprehensively characterise the TOI-1518 system by refining its orbital and physical parameters, and by investigating the chemical composition of the planetary atmosphere through transmission spectroscopy. We employed a joint Bayesian framework combining TESS photometry, HARPS-N high-resolution spectroscopy, and least-squares deconvolution profiles to break stellar geometrical degeneracies. We then applied single-line and cross-correlation function (CCF) transmission spectroscopy across theoretical templates. By anchoring the stellar projected rotational velocity ($v \sin i_\star \approx 79.7$ km s$^{-1}$), we confirmed the nearly polar orbit ($λ\approx 238^\circ$) and the theoretically predicted nodal precession ($\mathrm{d}i/\mathrm{d}t \approx 0.15^\circ$ yr$^{-1}$). We revealed an atmospheric Rossiter-McLaughlin (RM) effect and a bulk atmospheric blue-shift of $\approx -7.0$ km s$^{-1}$. Through transmission spectroscopy, we detected H I, C I, Na I, Ca I, Sc II, Ti II, V II, Cr I, Fe I, Fe II, Ni I, Sr II, Y II, Eu II, and W I. This marks the first detection of H I, C I, Sc II, V II, Sr II, Y II, Eu II, and W I in this planet, and the first ever detection of Eu II and W I in an exoplanetary atmosphere. Inconsistencies in the Na I doublet shifts suggest likely stellar contamination. Furthermore, time-resolved CCF analysis revealed morning-to-evening limb asymmetries for species like Mg I and Ba I, hinting at night-side cold traps. The atmosphere of TOI-1518 b exhibits a rich chemical inventory shaped by intense irradiation and bulk circulation. Our results emphasize the necessity of simultaneously modelling stellar line morphology and planetary tracks to accurately interpret atmospheric signals under strong RM effects.

title: Hints of planet formation in progress around DR Tau from observations with LBT SHARK-NIR and SHARK-VIS
comment: 12 pages; 10 Figures; Accepted for publications on A&A
summary: Protoplanetary disks are the primary sites of planet formation. However, the direct imaging of protoplanets still embedded within their parental disks remains a significant challenge, with only a small number of confirmed detections to date and several candidates awaiting verification. We search for embedded planets in the protoplanetary disk of the young star DRTau by targeting accretion signatures from forming sub-stellar objects. Using narrow-band imaging, we observe both visible Halpha and near-infrared Paschen-beta (Pabeta) emission to identify actively accreting companions. To this end, we performed high-contrast observations of DRTau using the SHARK-VIS (0.40-0.95 micron) and SHARK-NIR (0.96-1.70 micron) imagers at the LBT. The study uses a combination of narrow-band filters to isolate accretion signatures and broad-band filters for multi-wavelength characterization in both the visible and near-infrared. Our observations recover the primary disk structures previously identified in the literature, albeit at low signal-to-noise (S/N). We identify two compact features with S/N between 6 and 13 in both narrow- and broad-band filters. The first, an elongated structure, matches previous SPHERE detections, while the second, more compact feature, is now confirmed despite its low S/N in earlier datasets. A comparison over a seven-year baseline confirms the stability of both structures. Their observed orbital motion is consistent with Keplerian rotation, potentially suggesting the presence of an undetected planetary-mass companion (few MJup) at the location of the second feature. However, our analysis does not confirm Halpha or Pabeta emission originating from localized accretion. Instead, we conclude that the observed flux is likely stellar light reflected by dust at these locations and discuss alternative mechanisms that could account for such detections.

title: 2026 QQ8: Earth's temporary flyby of maximum lunation
summary: Aims: On a rare occasion, asteroids are temporarily captured by the Earth to become the planet's interim companions. The discovery of asteroid 2026~QQ$_8$ provided an opportunity to study this class of objects, adding to the sparse discovery catalogue of Earth's temporary companions. Methods: We performed astrometric, photometric, and dynamical studies of 2026~QQ$_8$, and measured its solar radiation pressure signal to discern between a natural and an artificial origin. Results: We find 2026 QQ$_8$ to be of natural origin, with solar radiation pressure signal commensurable with natural objects and spectrophotometry of an S-type object. 2026 QQ$_8$ is Earth's third discovered otemporarily-captured companion on a flyby orbit, and the first long-duration one, owing this to being on the so-called "orbit of maximum lunation". Its unusual orbit lies close to the theoretical upper duration limit of an object captured in the Earth-Moon system, and has now been observed for the first time.

title: Carving the Neptunian desert as a function of stellar mass and lifetime XUV irradiation
comment: 17 pages, 11 figures, 4 tables. Accepted for publication in MNRAS
summary: The Neptunian desert is a prominent feature in the exoplanet population, thought to arise from both XUV-driven photoevaporation and tidal circularisation following high-eccentricity migration. However, the extent to which each mechanism contributes, and where, remains uncertain. We examine the desert as a function of stellar type as a test of these mechanisms. We determine the desert boundaries for subsamples of F, G, K, and M-hosted planets for radius against period, semi-major axis, bolometric instellation, and lifetime XUV irradiation. Going from F to M, we observe shifts in the boundary between 2.2-7.5 R$_\oplus$ towards shorter orbital periods, smaller orbital distances, and much smaller instellations. These shifts match changes in lifetime XUV irradiation as a function of stellar mass at fixed period, semi-major axis, and bolometric instellation, evidence towards a photoevaporative origin for the desert at these radii. This is especially the case for orbital period, where the boundary should be invariant across stellar types under the high-eccentricity mechanism. In lifetime XUV space, we see significant overlap in the boundary across stellar types up to 7.5 R$_\oplus$. While this could be further evidence towards the XUV-driven mechanism in this regime, our uncertainties cannot rule out a shift in the boundary of the magnitude expected under the high-eccentricity mechanism. Overall, our results suggest a photoevaporative origin of the Neptunian desert up to sub-Saturn radii, but increased sample sizes, especially for M-hosted, Neptune-sized planets, will help distinguish further between the mechanisms.
